appraisal_events.evidence: Norpois's ornate speech ('l'Académie est très routinière... j'estime que la sagesse est de s'abstenir') is, beneath its courtesy, a refusal to help; the prince himself concludes 'Le cordon de Saint-André est une erreur... les négociations n'ont pas fait un pas... Je n'ai pas mis la main sur la bonne clef,' and later, gravely ill, worries only about being nominated before he dies.
appraisal_events.explanation: Norpois's flattering, theatrical language (delivered 'comme un vieil acteur qui veut juger de son effet') masks a real rebuff of the prince's Institut candidacy; the prince's own private recognition of failure, and his later petty anxiety about dying before nomination, confirm the passage's dominant diminishing movement toward him.

appraisal_events.evidence: The narrator likens the reasoning of 'M. de Norpois et le prince allemand' to that of a kept woman who says 'Ne parlons pas d'argent' or to 'les apaches,' arguing diplomats decode self-interest beneath official words just as one decodes a cocotte's true meaning.
appraisal_events.explanation: The elevated dignity of Norpois's diplomatic manner is ironically undercut by an explicit comparison to the mercenary calculations of kept women and street toughs, even as the same passage credits diplomats with real (if cynical) insight; the comparison implicates the unnamed prince equally.

status_effects.explanation: His campaign for a seat at the Institut is effectively declined despite Norpois's gracious phrasing, and he privately recognizes the negotiation has failed to advance.

The narrator's ironic comparison of his polished diplomatic rhetoric to the self-interested language of kept women and apaches undercuts the dignity of his self-presentation, even while crediting his practical shrewdness.

ambiguities: The unnamed 'prince' (once specified as 'prince von ***', a redacted German title) does not match any reference-sheet entry, including the unrelated 'prince de Guermantes'; his surface forms are recorded verbatim as unresolved.

The discrediting comparison in E2 is explicitly attributed to 'M. de Norpois et le prince allemand' jointly; the event's single target field names Norpois, but the same discredit applies to the prince as well.
